subject: Neptune pricing: per-token definitions and streaming slab proposal
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@neptune-analytics.com>
Cc: Maya Rios <maya.rios@neptune-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro: Pricing and usage metrics for Neptune POC

Hi Maya / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time today — excited about the POC scope and the telemetry use case you showed. Before we lock the commercial terms, a couple quick clarifications on how Neptune expects us to define billable usage so the numbers in the POC estimate line up with procurement's model:

- Do you require per-call invoices (i.e., individual request billing) or are you OK with session-aggregated measurement for streaming use cases?
- For streaming (long-running assistant sessions), are you comfortable with slab-based rounding (e.g., 10 token increments) or do you need exact per-token accounting?
- Any internal chargeback / internal-tooling constraints we should be aware of (e.g., you can't accept fractional tokens or sub-10 token increments)?

I'll attach a quick pricing workbook with the POC commit and a couple of variants. If helpful, we can propose a short contract paragraph describing the metric and rounding we use.

I can follow up with proposed language and a draft sheet by Tuesday.

Best,
Sean
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: Neptune-Proofed-Pricing.xlsx (spreadsheet), streaming-token-addendum.pdf (draft addendum)

From: Maya Rios <maya.rios@neptune-analytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Pricing and usage metrics for Neptune POC

Thanks Sean — quick answers from procurement side:

- We prefer invoices that reconcile at the invoice level (monthly). For streaming sessions we need to be able to attribute total billable units per session for internal showback, not necessarily per-call line items.
- Our auditors are strict: we cannot accept rounded bills that would materially change spend in our accounting. That said, we're open to small, clearly documented rounding rules for streaming sessions if they are capped.
- Minimum billing granularity: we currently bill internally on 10-token increments for other vendors, so if you can align with that it will simplify our internal reconciliation.

A couple follow-ups: what does Redwood mean by "streaming token count" for sessions that have partial tokens in their last chunk? And how do you treat cancellations or aborted sessions (do you bill partial-session tokens or zero them out)?

—Maya
Maya Rios
Head of Procurement, Neptune Analytics
maya.rios@neptune-analytics.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Neptune — rounding / streaming questions (need language + pricing tweak)

Laura / Aditya,

Forwarding procurement's note below. Two asks:

1) Laura — can you propose succinct contract language that:
   - defines "billable tokens" (what we count)
   - explicitly states rounding rules for streaming sessions (Procurement prefers 10-token increments)
   - addresses aborted/cancelled sessions (we generally bill consumed tokens; want to confirm wording)

2) Aditya — can you run a version of the POC sheet where streaming sessions are aggregated per-session, and the per-session totals are rounded up to the nearest 10 tokens (to match Neptune's internal showback). We may offer a small concession on list price if they accept session-slab rounding (easier for them).

Procurement also flagged they can't accept rounding that materially changes spend — let's include an explicit cap: rounding may increase billed tokens by no more than 0.5% of total monthly consumed tokens, otherwise we'll fall back to per-token exact accounting for that month.

Appreciate quick turn — they're aiming to finalize POC commercial terms by EOW.

Thanks,
Sean

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-03T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Neptune — rounding / streaming questions (need language + pricing tweak)

Sean / Aditya — draft language below. Keep it intentionally short; procurement prefers bright-line rules they can map to a reconciliation process.

Suggested contract clause (streaming & rounding):

1) Definitions: "Billable Token" means a unit of model consumption equivalent to one model input or output token as recorded by Redwood's usage metering system.

2) Measurement Method: For non-streaming requests, Billable Tokens are measured per request and billed on a per-token basis. For streaming sessions (persistent assistant sessions spanning multiple requests), Billable Tokens for the session will be aggregated at the session level.

3) Rounding Rule: When session-level aggregation is used, the session total will be rounded up to the nearest 10-token increment for billing purposes, provided that the aggregate effect of rounding across all sessions in a single monthly invoice does not increase billed tokens by more than 0.5% of the total measured tokens for that invoice period. If the rounding uplift exceeds 0.5% in any invoice period, Redwood will instead bill on an exact per-token basis for that period and notify the Customer in the invoice notes.

4) Aborted or Cancelled Sessions: Tokens consumed by an aborted or cancelled session (i.e., sessions terminated by the client before explicit end-of-session) will be billed for actual consumed tokens at session aggregation and rounding rules above. Tokens reserved but never consumed (e.g., pre-allocated KV cache reservations) are not billable.

5) Audit & Dispute Rights: Customer may request a one-time invoice audit per 12-month period. If a billing dispute results in a material adjustment (>1% of the invoice value), Redwood will reimburse the adjustment and provide a report of token measurement for the disputed period.

If this looks good I can trim further. Note we should push to avoid multi-month caps that lock us into fixed rounding behavior — the 0.5% escape hatch should be helpful.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rios <maya.rios@neptune-analytics.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@neptune-analytics.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Neptune pricing: per-token definitions and streaming slab proposal

Maya — thanks for the quick direction. Per procurement's preferences, here's what Redwood is prepared to put into the POC SOW and the underlying commercial term sheet:

- Measurement: Standard per-request per-token metering for non-streaming calls. Streaming sessions will be measured at session granularity and the session total will be rounded up to the nearest 10-token increment for billing.
- Cap on rounding uplift: Rounding may not increase billed tokens by more than 0.5% on any monthly invoice. If uplift >0.5% in any invoice period, Redwood will revert to exact per-token billing for that period and include a note in the invoice.
- Aborted/Cancelled sessions: Billed for actual consumed tokens (session-aggregated) and then subject to the same rounding rule. Reserved but unused allocations are not billed.
- Pricing offer: For the Neptune POC we propose a 12-month trial commit of 1.2M tokens/month at a 22% discount to list for hosted API (per-token). If Neptune wants exact per-token billing regardless of uplift, we can keep the same pricing but reduce the discount to 20% (since exact billing increases our metering overhead).

Attached: Neptune-Proofed-Pricing.xlsx (POC commit scenarios) and streaming-token-addendum.pdf (proposed clause text).

If this matches procurement's needs, I'll prep a short SOW and a DocuSign link for signature (I included a HubSpot deal and pricing sheet in the related links). Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to finalize.

Best,
Sean
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: Neptune-Proofed-Pricing.xlsx, streaming-token-addendum.pdf
